greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is the beginning and the end of all things, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the light that shines in the darkness. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the hope of those who wait for the dawn. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the promise of the wedding feast of the Lamb. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Stand erect and raise your heads because your redemption is at hand.
homily:
In the Book of Revelation, we encounter an image of staggering, final weight: a mighty angel takes a millstone, a massive, heavy thing, and throws it into the sea. It sinks. It is gone. The clamor of the city—the music, the work, the voices of the bride and groom—is silenced. It is a scene of profound ending. We see the world as it is—fragile, shifting, and ultimately temporary. We look at the great cities of our own lives, the structures we have built with such care, and we realize that the foundations of this earth are not meant to be our permanent home. 

I want you to hold onto this image today: the millstone. It is a heavy, circular thing, meant for grinding grain, meant for the daily bread of life. But here, it becomes an instrument of finality. It is a reminder that there is a threshold between the world of time and the world of eternity. Think of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way he moved through this life with such a bright, inquisitive spirit. He was a boy who understood the mechanics of things, who looked at the complex systems of the world—the flight paths of airplanes, the logic of code, the architecture of the future—with a mind that was always reaching, always soaring. He was a boy who built his own internal world with the bricks of curiosity and the mortar of kindness. He was a boy who, in his fifteen years, lived with a heart that was already tuned to something higher. He was a boy who could look at his father and say, with a smile that carried the warmth of a summer day, 'I love you,' and mean it with the entirety of his being. 

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: five months have passed. The calendar page turns, but the heart often stays in the room where he last smiled. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the quick laugh, the bright smile, the way he would share his dreams of 'con chim airlines'—are suddenly met with an empty space. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary day. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are not a lack of faith; they are the language of love that has no place left to go. 

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. You are not to blame for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus tells his disciples that when they see the world shaken, when they see the signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars, they should not be afraid. He says, 'Stand erect and raise your heads because your redemption is at hand.' This is the hinge of the mystery. The world may be in dismay, the sea may roar, but the Christian is called to a different posture. We are not to cower. We are to stand. Why? Because our redemption is not a distant hope; it is the person of Jesus Christ, who is already standing on the other side of the veil, waiting to welcome us home. Think of Benjamin’s heart—that boy who, unprompted, wanted to hand over his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it; the offering itself was the testimony. It was the pure, unadulterated desire to be a blessing to someone else. That is the wisdom that cannot be refuted. That is the life that speaks louder than any argument. Ben’s life is a testimony that love is the only thing that survives the fire. The millstone sinks, but the love we give on earth is the only thing that remains when we pass through the veil. It is purified, it is made eternal, and it is what we carry into the presence of the Lamb.

Consider the image of the millstone again. If the millstone represents the weight of the world, then the Wedding Feast of the Lamb represents the lightness of God. In the Book of Revelation, the angel says, 'Blessed are those who have been called to the wedding feast of the Lamb.' Benjamin is at that feast now. He is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven. He is fully alive, fully restored, and fully embraced by the Father. He is the boy who loved to dream, the boy who giggled at the idea of his own airline, the boy who looked at the world with such profound curiosity. He is all of that, and he is with the God of the living. He is the firstfruits of the promise, waiting for the day when the family of four is whole again. He is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where you and Ben were standing outside room 419, and he said with that earnest, familiar voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart. You are the one who carries his laughter forward. You are the one who keeps the melody alive.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. The Lamb who was slain is the Lamb who is risen, and he is the one who promises that one day, every tear will be wiped away, and we will see clearly that love was the only thing that ever mattered. The God of the living is the God who is with you right now in this very room, in the silence, in the ache, and in the hope that refuses to die.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may He let His face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may He give you His peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the light and peace of Christ, we pray to the Lord.
For all who are grieving today, especially Benjamin’s family, that God may console them with His presence and fill their hearts with the hope of the resurrection, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
I, John, saw another angel coming down from heaven,
having great authority,
and the earth became illumined by his splendor.
He cried out in a mighty voice:
“Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great.
She has become a haunt for demons.
She is a cage for every unclean spirit,
a cage for every unclean bird,
a cage for every unclean and disgusting beast.”

A mighty angel picked up a stone like a huge millstone
and threw it into the sea and said:

“With such force will Babylon the great city be thrown down,
and will never be found again.
No melodies of harpists and musicians,
flutists and trumpeters,
will ever be heard in you again.
No craftsmen in any trade
will ever be found in you again.
No sound of the millstone
will ever be heard in you again.
No light from a lamp
will ever be seen in you again.
No voices of bride and groom
will ever be heard in you again.
Because your merchants were the great ones of the world,
all nations were led astray by your magic potion.”

After this I heard what sounded like
the loud voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying:

“Alleluia!
Salvation, glory, and might belong to our God,
for true and just are his judgments.
He has condemned the great harlot
who corrupted the earth with her harlotry.
He has avenged on her the blood of his servants.”

They said a second time:

“Alleluia!  Smoke will rise from her forever and ever.”

Then the angel said to me,

“Write this:
Blessed are those who have been called
to the wedding feast of the Lamb.”

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples:
“When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies,
know that its desolation is at hand.
Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains.
Let those within the city escape from it,
and let those in the countryside not enter the city,
for these days are the time of punishment
when all the Scriptures are fulfilled.
Woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days,
for a terrible calamity will come upon the earth
and a wrathful judgment upon this people.
They will fall by the edge of the sword
and be taken as captives to all the Gentiles;
and Jerusalem will be trampled underfoot by the Gentiles
until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.

"There will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars,
and on earth nations will be in dismay,
perplexed by the roaring of the sea and the waves.
People will die of fright
in anticipation of what is coming upon the world,
for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man
coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
But when these signs begin to happen,
stand erect and raise your heads
because your redemption is at hand.”

day: Thursday of the Thirty-fourth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
